sections.advice: Jindabyne → Thredbo is 37 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.

scenicChapters.title: Alpine Way
scenicChapters.narrative: For 57 km this is Alpine Way, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Alpine Way
scenicChapters.narrative: Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it. The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 1582 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Dead Horse Gap → Khancoban
scenicChapters.narrative: 69 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it — this is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

alpine-way.story: 134 km from Jindabyne to the finish, about 1 h 52 of riding. On the way it passes Thredbo and Dead Horse Gap. The highest point is about 1,600 m. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.

scenicChapters.title: Villa de Leyva Road
scenicChapters.narrative: Height already gained and held. The road stays near 2820 m for 76 km instead of surrendering it to the next valley — exposed ground: wind matters more here than gradient. Nothing blocks it.

scenicChapters.title: Villa de Leyva Road
scenicChapters.narrative: 50 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it. This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

villa-de-leyva-road.story: From Tunja it runs 172 km to Ráquira; allow about 3 h 18 of riding. It goes by way of Arcabuco and Villa de Leyva. The highest point is 2,820 m. The line favours views over speed.
